from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Setup: Elastic Collisions", [
            "Two blocks collide on a frictionless surface.",
            "Momentum and energy are conserved in elastic collisions.",
            "Consider a massive block hitting a small one."
        ])
        
        # Define objects using SVG assets
        block_asset = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg"
        block1 = SVGMobject(block_asset, color="#FF0000", fill_opacity=0.8)
        block2 = SVGMobject(block_asset, color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=0.8)
        
        # Position objects using feedback constraints
        self.place_at_grid(block1, "D3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(block2, "D6", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Velocity labels
        v1 = MathTex("v_1", color="#FF0000")
        v2 = MathTex("v_2", color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(v1, "B3", scale_factor=0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(v2, "B6", scale_factor=0.7)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(block1), FadeIn(block2), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        
        # Flash collision point
        collision_pt = SVGMobject(block_asset, color="#FFFFFF").scale(0.3).move_to((block1.get_right() + block2.get_left()) / 2)
        self.play(Flash(collision_pt))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.play(
            block1.animate.shift(RIGHT * 1.0),
            block2.animate.shift(LEFT * 0.5),
            FadeIn(v1), FadeIn(v2)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Add a wall behind the smaller block.",
            "The block bounces between the wall and big block.",
            "A counter tracks the total number of collisions."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Collision Count", lecture_lines)
        
        # Load asset and objects
        wall = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/wall.svg")
        wall.set_color("#AAAAAA")
        self.place_at_grid(wall, "E2", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        small_block = Circle(radius=0.3, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(small_block, "E3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        big_block = Circle(radius=0.6, color=RED, fill_opacity=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(big_block, "E5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        counter_label = Text("Collisions:", font_size=24)
        counter_val = Integer(0, font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        counter = VGroup(counter_label, counter_val).arrange(RIGHT)
        self.place_in_area(counter, "B4", "B6", scale_factor=0.9)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(FadeIn(wall))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(RED)
        # Bouncing animation path
        path = VMobject()
        path.set_points_smoothly([self.grid["E3"], self.grid["E4"], self.grid["E3"]])
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(small_block, path), run_time=2)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(FadeIn(counter))
        
        # Update counter simulation
        current_counter_val = 0
        for i in range(1, 4):
            new_val = Integer(i, font_size=24, color=YELLOW)
            new_val.move_to(counter_val.get_center())
            self.play(Transform(counter_val, new_val), run_time=0.5)
            self.wait(0.2)
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Increasing mass ratios change the collision count.",
            "Mass ratio 100 yields 31 collisions.",
            "Mass ratio 10,000 yields 314 collisions.",
            "The count converges to digits of Pi.",
            "This links simple physics to transcendental numbers."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Mathematical Bridge", lecture_lines)
        
        # Assets
        billiard_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/billiard.svg")
        blocks_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/blocks.svg")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF6666"))
        self.place_at_grid(billiard_icon, "A3", scale_factor=0.5)
        label_r = Text("R", color="#00FFFF").next_to(billiard_icon, RIGHT)
        formula = MathTex(r"N \approx \pi \sqrt{\frac{M_1}{M_2}}").scale(0.8)
        self.place_in_area(formula, "A2", "B5", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(billiard_icon), Write(label_r), Write(formula))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#66FF66"))
        self.place_at_grid(blocks_icon, "C3", scale_factor=0.5)
        count_31 = Text("31", color=WHITE).next_to(blocks_icon, RIGHT)
        self.play(FadeIn(blocks_icon), Write(count_31))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#6666FF"))
        count_314 = Text("314", color=WHITE).next_to(blocks_icon, RIGHT)
        self.play(Transform(count_31, count_314))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FFFF66"))
        pi_text = Text(r"$\approx 3.14$", color="#FF00FF").scale(1.2)
        self.place_in_area(pi_text, "C2", "D5", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(formula, pi_text))
        self.play(pi_text.animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===

outline.topic: The Mystery of Pi in Block Collisions
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students in Physics or Computer Science

sections.title: The Setup: Elastic Collisions
sections.content: Introduce the physical system: Two blocks on a frictionless surface. Block A (mass M1) is moving toward Block B (mass M2, stationary). Define the conservation of momentum and kinetic energy as prerequisites for elastic collisions.
sections.example: A massive elephant (Block A, 100kg) approaching a tiny mouse (Block B, 1kg). When they collide elastically, the mouse zips away while the elephant barely slows down.

sections.title: Visualizing the Collision Count
sections.content: Introduce a wall behind the mouse. The mouse bounces off the elephant, then the wall, then back into the elephant. Visualize the state space as a 2D plot where axes represent the velocities of the two blocks.
sections.example: An animation showing the mouse bouncing back and forth between the wall and the elephant, with a digital counter ticking up the total number of collisions.

sections.title: The Mathematical Bridge
sections.content: Explain that as the mass ratio M1/M2 approaches infinity (e.g., 100^n), the total number of collisions converges to the first digits of Pi. Explain this via the reflection of a trajectory in a wedge-shaped phase space.
sections.example: If M1/M2 = 100, the system yields 31 collisions (approximating 3.14...). If M1/M2 = 10,000, it yields 314 collisions.

sections.title: Geometric Interpretation
sections.content: Connect the physics to geometry: The angle of the trajectory in phase space corresponds to the ratio of the masses. The collisions are reflections within a triangle, and the total count measures the slope required to 'escape' the wedge.
sections.example: A graphical overlay showing a light beam bouncing inside a V-shaped mirror, where the number of reflections reveals the precise angle of the wedge.

sections.title: Conclusion and Intuition
sections.content: Summarize how discrete physical events (collisions) map to transcendental numbers (Pi). Emphasize that conservation laws act as a constraint that forces the system to 'calculate' Pi.
sections.example: Final animation: A clockwork mechanism where the number of gears turning represents digits of Pi, summarizing that the universe performs 'computation' through simple physical interactions.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: Blocks are positioned too close to the left-side text, creating visual clutter and reducing separation between text and animation. Fix: Line 59: self.place_at_grid(block1, 'C3', scale_factor=0.8); Line 60: self.place_at_grid(block2, 'C6', scale_factor=0.8) (line=59, object=block1, block2)
issues.resolution_note: Positioned blocks according to feedback.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: Velocity labels (v1, v2) are too close to the blocks, risking potential overlap with collision markers. Fix: Line 61: self.place_at_grid(v1, 'B3', scale_factor=0.7); Line 62: self.place_at_grid(v2, 'B6', scale_factor=0.7) (line=61, object=velocity_labels)
issues.resolution_note: Positioned velocity labels at B3 and B6.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: Inconsistent vertical alignment between the massive block and the small block complicates the visual hierarchy. Fix: Line 63: self.place_at_grid(block1, 'D3', scale_factor=1.0); Line 64: self.place_at_grid(block2, 'D6', scale_factor=0.6) (line=63, object=block1, block2)
issues.resolution_note: Adjusted vertical alignment/scale to D3 (1.0) and D6 (0.6).

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The animation elements (wall and blocks) occupy row C, which creates visual clutter near the lecture lines and restricts vertical breathing room. Fix: Line 56, 59, 62: self.place_in_area('wall', 'D2', 'D2', scale_factor=0.8); self.place_at_grid('small_block', 'D3', scale_factor=0.8); self.place_at_grid('big_block', 'D5', scale_factor=0.8) (line=56, object=wall, small_block, big_block)
issues.resolution_note: Applied suggested grid positioning (E2, E3, E5).

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The counter is positioned too high and right, potentially conflicting with title elements if the screen aspect ratio is narrow. Fix: Line 67: self.place_in_area('counter', 'B4', 'B6', scale_factor=0.9) (line=67, object=counter)
issues.resolution_note: Positioned counter in area B4-B6.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The current layout leaves the lower half of the screen (rows E and F) completely underutilized, leading to a top-heavy visual weight. Fix: Line 56-67: Shift all active elements down one grid row (e.g., wall to E2, blocks to E3/E5) to balance the frame. (line=56, object=all_elements)
issues.resolution_note: Shifted all elements down to rows E and balanced with counter at B.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: The formulas are positioned too far to the right, creating a visual imbalance and wasting the central negative space. Fix: Line 5: self.place_in_area(formula, 'A2', 'B5', scale_factor=0.8) (line=5, object=formula)
issues.resolution_note: Fixed formula positioning.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: The conservation law equation is positioned too low, causing excessive vertical dispersion from the first formula. Fix: Line 6: self.place_in_area(cons_law, 'C2', 'D5', scale_factor=0.8) (line=6, object=cons_law)
issues.resolution_note: Fixed equation positioning.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: Potential for visual clutter due to lack of distinct separation between the two physics equations. Fix: Line 7: Use self.place_in_area(cons_law, 'D2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.8) to maintain clear grid hierarchy between the top formula and bottom equation. (line=7, object=cons_law)
issues.resolution_note: Fixed hierarchy positioning.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: The animation occupies the same central grid space (B2-E5) for all three assets, causing severe visual clutter and overlap. Fix: Line 63: self.place_in_area(circle, 'A2', 'C4', scale_factor=0.5) (line=63, object=circle)
issues.resolution_note: Fixed clutter by repositioning the circle to A2-C4.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: The wedge and trajectory are stacked on top of each other, obscuring details and creating an unreadable visual composition. Fix: Line 73: self.place_in_area(wedge, 'D2', 'F4', scale_factor=0.6) (line=73, object=wedge)

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: The dot is currently placed too close to the center of the animation mass, failing to highlight the specific trajectory endpoint clearly. Fix: Line 87: self.place_at_grid(dot, 'D5', scale_factor=0.8) (line=87, object=dot)
issues.resolution_note: Fixed dot position by placing it at D5.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: The gear animation at B3 is too close to the upper-right corner and feels disconnected from the lecture text on the left. Fix: Line 62: self.place_at_grid(gear, 'B5', scale_factor=0.8) (line=62, object=gear)

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: The pi_text at E3 occupies central grid space and risks visual clutter with potential future animations. Fix: Line 71: self.place_at_grid(pi_text, 'E5', scale_factor=1.0) (line=71, object=pi_text)

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: Inconsistent vertical spacing between animation objects creates an unbalanced layout on the right side of the screen. Fix: Line 71: self.place_in_area(pi_text, 'D4', 'F6', scale_factor=0.9) (line=71, object=pi_text)
